items.description: Analyze repository structure, available tooling, and agent capabilities
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/repo_analysis.md documenting: (a) all modules in .archivara/ and .opencode/ with their purposes, (b) available tools (semantic_scholar, concept_evolve) and their commands (evolve/probe/reframe/walk and search/citations/references/recommend/graph/bibtex), (c) agent roles defined in opencode.json (orchestrator, researcher, writer, reviewer, concept_worker), (d) empty scaffolds (figures/, results/) to be populated. File must be at least 300 words.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive web-based literature review on N-body gravity simulation methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Use web search and Semantic Scholar to survey at least 4 sub-topics: (a) classical direct-summation N-body methods and softening techniques, (b) hierarchical tree codes (Barnes-Hut) and fast multipole methods (Greengard-Rokhlin), (c) symplectic integrators (Stormer-Verlet, leapfrog, Yoshida) and their conservation properties, (d) modern GPU-accelerated and parallel N-body solvers. Produce results/literature_review.md with at least 1500 words, structured sections for each sub-topic, and inline citations referencing entries in sources.bib.

items.description: Create and populate sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted references
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib exists at repo root with at least 10 valid BibTeX entries. Required entries include: Barnes & Hut 1986 (tree code), Verlet 1967 (integration method), Greengard & Rokhlin 1987 (FMM), Aarseth 2003 (gravitational N-body simulations textbook), at least 2 papers on symplectic integrators (e.g., Yoshida 1990, Wisdom & Holman 1991), at least 2 modern GPU/parallel N-body papers (post-2010), and at least 2 open-source N-body codebases (e.g., REBOUND, Gadget-2, NBODY6). Each entry must have author, title, year, and journal/booktitle fields.

items.description: Delegate citation-graph mining to literature-graph-miner subagent for cross-domain insights
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a literature-graph-miner subagent to traverse citation graphs seeded from Barnes & Hut 1986, Verlet 1967, and Greengard & Rokhlin 1987. Produce results/citation_graph_analysis.md containing: (a) at least 5 high-impact descendant papers (>500 citations each) with one-sentence summaries, (b) at least 3 cross-domain connections (e.g., molecular dynamics, electrostatics, cosmological simulation), (c) identification of 2 underexplored techniques transferable to a minimal gravity sim. File must reference specific paper IDs from Semantic Scholar.

items.description: Define problem scope, constraints, and success criteria for the minimal gravity simulation
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/problem_definition.md specifying: (a) particle count range (minimum 10 to 10000), (b) dimensionality (2D with optional 3D extension), (c) required integrators (Euler baseline + leapfrog minimum), (d) force solvers to implement (direct O(N^2) + at least one O(N log N) method), (e) performance target (real-time at 30fps for N <= 500 using direct solver), (f) accuracy target (energy conservation < 0.1% drift per 1000 steps with leapfrog), (g) language and dependencies (Python 3.10+, NumPy, Matplotlib), (h) visualization requirements (static plots + animated trajectories). Document must be at least 500 words.

items.description: Bootstrap concept-tree exploration for gravity simulation design space
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept_evolve with the 'evolve' command on the topic 'minimal N-body gravity simulation design space'. Verify that results/concept_evolve/tree/ contains at least 3 concept branches: (a) integration algorithms, (b) force calculation strategies, (c) spatial data structures. Each branch must have at least 2 leaf folders with concept.json and README.md files. The tree index at results/concept_evolve/tree/index.json must list all generated concept folders.

items.description: Implement direct-summation O(N^2) gravity solver with softening as the baseline
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gravity/direct.py implementing: (a) Particle class or dataclass with position (2D array), velocity (2D array), and mass (float), (b) Newtonian gravitational force calculation with Plummer softening parameter epsilon (default 0.01), (c) brute-force O(N^2) pairwise force accumulation returning acceleration array. Must include a unit test in tests/test_direct.py verifying: (i) two-body circular orbit semi-major axis error < 1% after 100 orbits, (ii) force symmetry (F_ij = -F_ji) for random 10-particle configuration, (iii) zero self-force. All tests must pass via pytest.

items.description: Implement Leapfrog (kick-drift-kick Stormer-Verlet) time integrator
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/integrators/leapfrog.py implementing the kick-drift-kick leapfrog scheme with function signature step(positions, velocities, masses, dt, force_fn) -> (new_positions, new_velocities). Also implement forward Euler in src/integrators/euler.py for comparison. Create tests/test_integrators.py verifying: (a) leapfrog energy drift < 0.1% over 10000 steps for a stable 2-body system with dt=0.001, (b) Euler energy diverges by > 5% over the same interval, (c) leapfrog is time-reversible (run forward N steps then backward N steps, position error < 1e-10). All tests pass via pytest.

items.description: Build metrics and benchmarking framework for timing, energy, and conservation tracking
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/metrics.py providing functions for: (a) compute_total_energy(positions, velocities, masses, softening) returning kinetic + potential energy as float, (b) compute_angular_momentum(positions, velocities, masses) returning L_z scalar for 2D, (c) TimingContext context manager recording wall-clock time per simulation step, (d) benchmark_sweep(solver_fn, integrator_fn, n_values, n_steps) that runs simulations for N in n_values and records timing/energy data. Output benchmark results to results/baseline_benchmarks.json with schema: {solver, integrator, N, steps, wall_time_seconds, initial_energy, final_energy, energy_error_pct}.

items.description: Create 2D visualization module for simulation validation and figure generation
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/visualization.py supporting: (a) plot_snapshot(positions, masses, filename) saving a 2D scatter plot with mass-proportional marker sizes to figures/, (b) plot_trajectories(trajectory_history, filename) saving particle paths as line plots, (c) plot_energy(time_array, energy_array, filename) saving energy-vs-time plot, (d) create_animation(trajectory_history, filename, fps=30) saving an animated GIF. Produce figures/baseline_two_body.png showing a stable two-body orbit snapshot and figures/baseline_energy.png showing energy conservation over 1000 steps. Both files must exist and be valid image files (>1KB each).

items.description: Delegate subagent analysis of baseline O(N^2) scaling and bottleneck identification
items.acceptance_criteria: Run baseline benchmarks for N in {10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000} using the direct solver + leapfrog integrator. Then launch a concept-tree-explorer subagent to analyze the timing data from results/baseline_benchmarks.json. Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/bottleneck_analysis/analysis.md identifying: (a) top 3 computational bottlenecks with quantified time percentages, (b) the N value where real-time (30fps) breaks down, (c) at least 3 specific optimization strategies referencing prior work from sources.bib with expected speedup estimates.

items.description: Implement Barnes-Hut quadtree O(N log N) gravity solver
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gravity/barnes_hut.py implementing: (a) QuadTree class with recursive spatial decomposition for 2D, (b) insert(particle) and compute_force(particle, theta=0.5) methods, (c) center-of-mass aggregation at internal nodes, (d) opening angle criterion (theta parameter) for multipole acceptance. Create tests/test_barnes_hut.py verifying: (i) force accuracy within 1% RMS of direct summation for 1000 random particles with theta=0.5, (ii) tree construction correctly partitions all particles (no lost particles), (iii) solver returns same result as direct for N=2. All tests pass.

items.description: Implement NumPy-vectorized O(N^2) force computation to eliminate Python loops
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gravity/vectorized.py using NumPy broadcasting to compute all pairwise forces without Python-level loops. Function signature: compute_accelerations(positions, masses, softening) -> accelerations. Create tests/test_vectorized.py verifying: (a) output matches direct.py to within 1e-12 relative error for 100 random particles, (b) achieves at least 10x wall-clock speedup over direct.py for N=1000 (measured via src/metrics.py). Append vectorized benchmark results to results/baseline_benchmarks.json.

items.description: Implement adaptive timestep control based on acceleration magnitudes
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/integrators/adaptive.py implementing timestep adaptation using the Aarseth criterion (dt proportional to sqrt(softening / |acceleration|)). Must support both per-particle individual timesteps and global adaptive timestep modes. Create tests/test_adaptive.py verifying: (a) at least 2x speedup over fixed-timestep leapfrog for a collapsing Plummer sphere scenario with N=100, (b) energy conservation within 0.5% over the collapse, (c) timestep correctly decreases during close encounters. All tests pass.

items.description: Concept-tree evolution exploring optimization strategies beyond Barnes-Hut
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept_evolve 'evolve' command on topic 'optimization strategies for N-body gravity beyond Barnes-Hut tree codes'. Verify results/concept_evolve/tree/ is updated with at least 4 new concept folders evaluating: particle-mesh (PM/P3M), fast multipole method (FMM-lite), spatial hashing, and at least one unconventional approach (e.g., learned force approximation, stochastic subsampling). Each folder must contain concept.json with a viability_score (0-10) field. Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/optimizations/ranking.md ranking all candidates with justification referencing sources.bib.

items.description: Implement the top-ranked novel optimization from concept-tree exploration
items.acceptance_criteria: Based on item_015 rankings, implement the highest-scored feasible optimization in src/gravity/<method_name>.py. Must include: (a) working implementation passing at least 2 correctness tests in tests/test_<method_name>.py, (b) documented time complexity in a docstring, (c) benchmark showing measurable improvement over vectorized.py for N >= 2000 particles (results appended to results/baseline_benchmarks.json). If no novel method outperforms Barnes-Hut, document why in results/concept_evolve/tree/optimizations/negative_result.md.

items.description: Delegate cross-domain reframing of gravity simulation problem via subagent
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a concept-tree-explorer subagent using concept_evolve 'reframe' on 'efficient many-body gravitational force computation'. Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/cross_domain/reframings.md documenting at least 5 domain reframings (molecular dynamics, electrostatics, fluid SPH, graph neural network force fields, game-engine physics) with: (a) the key transferable insight from each domain, (b) at least 3 concrete actionable techniques that could be back-ported to improve the gravity sim, (c) references to relevant papers from sources.bib where available.

items.description: Run comprehensive scaling experiments across all solver implementations
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute benchmarks for N in {10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000} across all implemented solvers (direct, vectorized, Barnes-Hut, and any Phase 3 novel solver). For each (solver, N) pair, record: wall_time_seconds, energy_error_pct, angular_momentum_error_pct. Save structured results to results/scaling_experiments.json. Produce figures/scaling_comparison.png showing log-log wall-time vs N with fitted complexity curves (labeled O(N^2), O(N log N), etc.). The figure must contain at least 3 solver curves.

items.description: Run integrator accuracy comparison experiments on canonical test problems
items.acceptance_criteria: Compare Euler, fixed-step leapfrog, and adaptive-step leapfrog on three scenarios: (a) two-body Kepler orbit with eccentricity 0.5 for 100 orbits, (b) Pythagorean three-body problem (masses 3,4,5 at vertices of a right triangle) for 50 time units, (c) random 100-particle Plummer sphere for 100 dynamical times. Measure and record: relative energy drift, phase-space error (where analytical solution exists), and wall-clock time. Save to results/integrator_comparison.json. Produce figures/energy_conservation.png and figures/integrator_phase_space.png. Each figure must be a valid image file > 1KB.

items.description: Conduct Barnes-Hut opening-angle (theta) sensitivity analysis
items.acceptance_criteria: For N=1000 random Plummer-distributed particles, sweep theta in {0.0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0} (theta=0.0 should reduce to direct summation). Measure: RMS force error vs direct summation, wall-clock time per step, and cumulative energy error after 100 steps. Save to results/theta_sensitivity.json. Produce figures/theta_sensitivity.png showing dual-axis plot (force error on left y-axis, speedup factor on right y-axis, theta on x-axis). Identify and report the Pareto-optimal theta value yielding < 1% force error.

items.description: Reproduce a published N-body benchmark from the literature and compare quantitatively
items.acceptance_criteria: Select one benchmark from sources.bib (e.g., Plummer sphere cold collapse from Aarseth 2003, or a two-body regression test from REBOUND documentation). Implement the initial conditions exactly as described in the source. Run with at least 2 solvers and compare: (a) qualitative trajectory match (visual comparison figure in figures/benchmark_reproduction.png), (b) at least 2 quantitative metrics (e.g., half-mass radius evolution, virial ratio) compared against published values with percent error reported. Document in results/benchmark_reproduction.md with explicit citations to the source paper.

items.description: Delegate experiment synthesis: compare results against literature claims via subagent
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a literature-graph-miner subagent to cross-reference experimental results from items 018-021 against performance claims and accuracy benchmarks from papers in sources.bib. Produce results/literature_comparison.md containing: (a) a comparison table with at least 5 rows, each comparing one metric from this project against a published value (with paper citation, our value, their value, percent difference), (b) identification of where the minimal sim matches, exceeds, or falls short of published results, (c) at least 2 specific recommendations for improvement based on techniques found in the literature.

items.description: Write comprehensive technical report synthesizing all research findings
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/technical_report.md containing: (a) Abstract (150-300 words), (b) Introduction with problem motivation and contributions, (c) Related Work section citing at least 8 entries from sources.bib with comparative discussion, (d) Methods section describing all solver and integrator implementations with complexity analysis, (e) Results section with embedded figure references (at least 4 figures from figures/), (f) Discussion comparing performance and accuracy against prior work from sources.bib, (g) Conclusion with limitations and 3 concrete future work directions. Minimum 3000 words total.

items.description: Generate final concept-tree summary and research exploration map
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/final_summary.md synthesizing all concept-tree explorations from Phases 1-4. Must include: (a) text-based tree visualization showing all concept branches and their leaf nodes, (b) table of which branches were pursued vs pruned with one-sentence justification for each, (c) top 5 key insights discovered through concept evolution with cross-references to where each insight was applied, (d) at least 3 suggested future branches for continued research with expected value assessment (high/medium/low).

items.description: Update README.md with project overview, installation, and usage instructions
items.acceptance_criteria: README.md contains: (a) project title 'Minimal N-Body Gravity Simulation' and one-paragraph description, (b) installation instructions (Python version, pip install from requirements.txt), (c) usage examples showing how to run each solver (direct, vectorized, Barnes-Hut) with sample commands, (d) summary table of key results (solver, N, time, energy error) with links to figures/, (e) repository structure diagram showing src/, tests/, results/, figures/ layout, (f) references section pointing to sources.bib. Must be at least 400 words.

items.description: Create reproducibility package with pinned dependencies and automated pipeline
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce: (a) requirements.txt listing all Python dependencies with pinned versions (at minimum: numpy, matplotlib, pytest), (b) run_all.py script that executes the complete pipeline: run all tests (pytest), run all benchmarks, generate all figures, and output a summary to stdout. Running 'python run_all.py' must complete without errors and regenerate all JSON result files and PNG figures. (c) results/reproducibility_checklist.md confirming each artifact (list every expected file in results/ and figures/) can be regenerated from scratch.

items.description: Delegate final completeness and quality audit via subagent
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a concept-tree-explorer subagent to audit the entire repository. Produce results/final_audit.md with a pass/fail checklist verifying: (a) all 26 prior rubric items have corresponding output artifacts (list each item_id and its artifact path), (b) sources.bib has >= 10 entries and all are referenced in the technical report, (c) all figures referenced in the report exist in figures/ and are valid images > 1KB, (d) concept tree in results/concept_evolve/tree/ has >= 3 branches with >= 2 leaves each, (e) all tests pass via pytest, (f) run_all.py completes without errors. At least 22 of 26 prior items must pass for the audit to be considered successful.
